changes.after: A closure can keep access to a nearby variable after it is made.

before: A proc or lambda can use an outer local variable after creation. Ruby captures the binding rather than freezing the earlier scalar value.
If offset changes from 2 to 9 before the closure is called, the closure reads 9.
Sharing a captured array also allows shared mutation. Keeping a closure can keep referenced objects reachable.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
offset = 2
add = ->(value) { value + offset }
offset = 9
puts add.call(3)
```
Expected output or behavior: 12. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
